linux.mechanism: /etc/opt/mqm/mqinst.ini Installation: stanzas; version from the swidtag file name under each installation's FilePath; no dspmqver

macos.fallback: planned; the action answers a single unsupported status row on this OS
macos.mechanism: installer-metadata read, not yet wired on macOS (every product)

windows.mechanism: HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\IBM\\WebSphere MQ\\Installation\\<name> FilePath/VRMF in both registry views

caveats: **Only registered installations are listed.** IBM MQ comes from `mqinst.ini` on Linux and the `HKLM\SOFTWARE\IBM\WebSphere MQ\Installation` registry key on Windows, so an unpacked copy that was never registered with the operating system is not found, and `supported` with zero rows means none was found there. The directory the stanza points at is only read for its version.

**The Windows leg is measured on one install, the macOS leg is planned.** The Windows leg reads `HKLM\SOFTWARE\IBM\WebSphere MQ\Installation\<name>` values `FilePath` and `VRMF` in both registry views; the key and both names were confirmed on one real IBM MQ 9.4.5.0 install (Windows 10.0.26200, bare metal, 2026-11-24, read in an elevated administrator session) (`docs/samples/windows.txt`), not as a standard (non-administrator) user, as the service account, on another MQ version, on a 32-bit-only registration or with several installations. If another version spells the `FilePath` name differently the failure is loud, never silent: an installation subkey whose `FilePath` is absent, empty, oversized or not text is skipped and, when none has one, the answer is `windows:middleware:installation_key:malformed`; a `FilePath` the registry refuses is an access fault, not a spelling one: it is `windows:middleware:installation_key:permission_denied`, and one that failed to read in any other way is `windows:middleware:installation_key:unreadable`; either constrains the answer and leaves that installation without a row, the others being kept. A different spelling of `VRMF` is loud too, once it affects every row: when no installation that got a row has a `VRMF` value at all (every `VRMF` read answered absent), the answer is `windows:middleware:vrmf:malformed`, constrained, with the rows kept at version `-` and one log line per installation (`vrmf: missing`). The token needs every row to lack the value: an installation whose `VRMF` is absent beside a sibling that has one only gets `-` (logged, the answer stays `supported`), and a `VRMF` that is refused, failed, oversized, empty or not text only blanks that row's version, whatever the other rows hold. On a host without the product the key is absent and the answer is `supported` with zero rows, as it is for a key that is present with no subkey. `supported` with zero rows means none was found in that key, not that none is installed. macOS is planned and ships no leg: the action answers `status|ibm_mq|unsupported|macos:planned`, because which file registers an installation on macOS is not known without a capture.

**The `mqinst.ini` form is confirmed on one version.** IBM documents the file's location and content but states its format is not fixed and reserves `dspmqinst` as the interface, which this plugin never runs. The `Installation:` header and the `Name`, `Description`, `Identifier` and `FilePath` spellings are confirmed on one registered 9.4.5.0 install (Ubuntu debs) only; no `Primary` key is read or required. A version or platform that spells them differently surfaces as `linux:middleware:mqinst_ini:malformed` (content but no `Installation:` line, or a file in which no stanza has both `Name` and `FilePath`), never as a silent empty inventory. A stanza that lacks one of them beside at least one usable stanza is a data fault of that stanza: it is skipped, the agent logs one line for it (`mqinst_ini: malformed (stanza <n>)`), and the usable stanzas are kept with the answer still `supported`. The table after caveat 5 sets out which faults constrain the answer and which are only logged.

**The version comes from the product tag only.** The name is `ibm.com_IBM_MQ*-<v>.swidtag`, else exactly `IBM_MQ-<v>.mqtag`. Bundled-component tags (GSKit, JRE, Runtime, Messages_*) carry their own versions and never name the product, so a directory holding only component tags yields a row with version `-` and a logged `missing`, not a token. The `.swidtag` form is matched by prefix and trailing version only, so a component tag in `.swidtag` form (for example `ibm.com_IBM_MQ_GSKit-8.0.55.swidtag`) would be taken for the product and its version reported. No capture holds one: the captured components are `.mqtag` files, each image holds one `.swidtag`, and only developer-edition installs were captured (no licensed server RPM or DEB), so a licensed install may differ.

**A constrained answer keeps the stored IBM MQ rows and shows them as unconfirmed.** The installed-software sync reports a `constrained` answer as a status-only section for the `ibm_mq` source, carrying the status row's tokens and no rows. The server keeps the stored IBM MQ rows, shown as unconfirmed, until a read succeeds again and a full section confirms them; nothing is deleted and no other source is affected. The section's token is the only signal that the read failed rather than that no installation exists. To read the tokens on the device, run the `ibm_mq` action and read its status row. What constrains the answer and what is only logged, by read (the first rows are the Linux `mqinst.ini` read, the Windows rows follow) (a constrained answer carries the token as a status-only section and sends no rows, as above): | Read | Answer | Token | Rows returned | |---|---|---|---| | File absent | `supported` | `-` | none (none found) | | File denied, oversized, behind a symlink, on a network mount, refused or otherwise unreadable | `constrained` | `mqinst_ini:permission_denied`, `oversized`, `symlink_refused`, `network_fs_skipped` or `unreadable` | none | | More than 256 stanzas | `constrained` | `mqinst_ini:row_cap` | the first 256 | | Row, row-text or directory-entry budget out | `constrained` | `walk:row_cap` | those built before the cut | | Mount table unreadable | `constrained` | `mountinfo:unreadable` | as usual, guarded by the mounts read | | Windows: installation key absent in both registry views | `supported` | `-` | none (none found) | | Windows: key refused in either view | `constrained` | `installation_key:permission_denied` | those of the view that answered (none when neither did) | | Windows: key failed in either view in any other way, and neither view was refused (a refusal outranks a failure) | `constrained` | `installation_key:unreadable` | those of the view that answered (none when neither did) | | Windows: key present with no definitions.description: Reports installed IBM MQ installations on Linux and Windows: one row per installation (title, name, version, install path). On Linux it reads the /etc/opt/mqm/mqinst.ini `Installation:` stanzas and takes the version from the product tag file name under each installation's FilePath/swidtag. On Windows it reads the HKLM Installation subkeys in both registry views (FilePath and VRMF values; confirmed on one real IBM MQ 9.4.5.0 install, read in an elevated administrator session). No `dspmqver` process is started. A `supported` status with no rows means no registered installation was found; a `constrained` status means a read failed or was skipped and the list may be incomplete. macOS: planned; the action answers a single unsupported status row (`status|ibm_mq|unsupported|macos:planned`).

description: Installed middleware inventory from installer metadata (table-driven; IBM MQ)
how_it_works:
`middleware` answers one question per product: which installations of that product are registered on this host, and at what version. It is table-driven. Each product is one row of a compile-time table (`agents/shared/middleware_products.hpp`) that names, per OS, the place that lists the product's installations (a file, or a registry key) and where the version is read from; one generic runner turns a row into data rows, so adding a product adds a table row and one action, not new walking code. Today the table holds IBM MQ (`ibm_mq`). On Linux the runner parses the `Installation:` stanzas of `/etc/opt/mqm/mqinst.ini` (`Name` and `FilePath`, values trimmed because the real file pads `Description` with trailing spaces) and lists the file names in each installation's `<FilePath>/swidtag`. The version is read from a file NAME, never from file content: the product's own `ibm.com_IBM_MQ*-<v>.swidtag`, else exactly `IBM_MQ-<v>.mqtag`; the bundled component tags beside them (GSKit, JRE, Runtime, Messages) never name the product. The plugin never starts `dspmqver`, `dspmqinst` or any other process, opens every directory without following symlinks, and does not open a path on, under or containing a network mount that `/proc/self/mountinfo` listed when the action started. The one open that is not hop by hop is that run-start read of the mount table: its leaf is opened without following a link, but `/proc/self` is the kernel's own link to the agent's process directory and is followed (the same read the `runtimes` plugin makes). That guard is a snapshot: a network filesystem mounted after it is not seen, and if the table cannot be read in full the walk still runs, guarded only by the mounts that were read, and the answer is `constrained` with `linux:middleware:mountinfo:unreadable`. Each action writes one `status` row first, then zero or more installation rows, so an empty list is never inferred from silence. On Windows the runner reads the registry instead of files: every subkey of `HKLM\SOFTWARE\IBM\WebSphere MQ\Installation` is one installation, named by the subkey, with its install path from the subkey's `FilePath` value and its version from the `VRMF` value, in both the 64-bit and the 32-bit registry view (a name present in both views is listed once). Only `REG_SZ` and `REG_EXPAND_SZ` values are read, unexpanded, only under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE` (never a user hive), and only through the wide `Reg*W` calls. The key and both value names were confirmed on one real IBM MQ 9.4.5.0 install (Windows 10.0.26200, bare metal, 2026-11-24, read in an elevated administrator session) and the Windows leg is declared `supported` (caveat 2). On macOS the action answers a single `unsupported` status row. The plugin is read-only, does no vulnerability matching (a row is presence plus the version string the installer recorded) and does not detect copies that were unpacked without being registered.

### What you can decide with it

| Question | Linux | Windows | macOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which IBM MQ installations are registered on this host, and at what version? (`ibm_mq`) | One row per registered installation with product title, installation name, version and install path | The same row shape from the registry, with the version as the full `VRMF` string; key and value names confirmed on one real 9.4.5.0 install (caveat 2) | Nothing: one `unsupported` row, result status `UNAVAILABLE` |
| Is an out-of-support MQ version installed on this host? | Yes, by comparing the `version` column against your own support list; the plugin attaches no verdict | Yes, the same way, with the caveat above | Not answerable |

What a result proves. On Linux a row proves the installation is registered in `mqinst.ini` under that name and path; on Windows it proves a subkey with that name and a `FilePath` value exists under the installation key. When its `version` is not `-`, it also proves, on Linux, that a product tag carrying that version was in the installation's `swidtag` directory, and, on Windows, that the subkey's `VRMF` value held that text. A `-` version means, on Linux, that the directory was absent, unreadable or held no product tag (caveat 4) and, on Windows, that the `VRMF` value was absent, refused, failed, oversized, empty or not text (caveat 2); either way the row then proves the registration only, and a `-` on every Windows row is itself reported, as `windows:middleware:vrmf:malformed`. Neither proves the product is running or intact. `supported` with zero rows means no registered installation was found at the places this plugin reads (on Windows: the key is absent in both views, or present with no subkey); it does not mean none is installed (caveat 1), and a `supported` answer can omit an installation whose `mqinst.ini` stanza was unusable on Linux, or a subkey whose `FilePath` value is absent, empty, oversized or not text on Windows, which only the agent's log records (caveats 2 and 3). `constrained` means a read failed or was refused, so the rows may be incomplete, and the installed-software sync sends a status-only section that leaves the stored IBM MQ rows in place, shown as unconfirmed (caveat 5); read the reason tokens before trusting a negative. For the packaged-application view use `installed_apps`.

On Linux the middleware leg judges a path against the mount table before opening it. The network types come from the shared list in `agents/shared/network_fstype.hpp`, which also names `ncpfs`, `coda`, `smb2` and the network-backed FUSE clients `gcsfuse`, `goofys`, `blobfuse`, `blobfuse2`, `ossfs`, `obsfs`, `cosfs`, `juicefs`, `mfsmount`, `moosefs`, `lizardfs`, `seaweedfs`, `weed`, `curlftpfs`, `httpfs2`, `s3ql`, `onedrive`, `google-drive-ocamlfuse`, `davfs2` and `fuse-nfs` (a mount of those types is treated as a network mount); an unlisted FUSE subtype and a stacked filesystem over a network mount are not detected by this list.
name: middleware

columns.description: Row shape discriminator (the wire row's leading tag). Values: status (exactly one per result, always first), ibm_mq (one per installation found).
columns.name: row_kind

columns.description: Product display name, fixed per action (IBM MQ). Status rows: the action name.
columns.name: title

columns.description: Installation name: the mqinst.ini Name value (Linux) or the installation registry subkey name (Windows), for example Installation1. Status rows: the level (supported, constrained or unsupported).
columns.name: name

columns.description: Installation version taken from the product tag file name (ibm.com_IBM_MQ*-<v>.swidtag, else IBM_MQ-<v>.mqtag; component tags such as GSKit or Runtime never name the product), or "-" when it cannot be read. Linux: VRM (version.release.modification), the fix-pack level is not carried, so a fix pack 9.3.5.1 reports 9.3.5. Windows: the VRMF registry value as the installer wrote it. Status rows: the comma-joined failure tokens, or -.
columns.name: version

columns.description: Absolute path of the installation (the mqinst.ini FilePath value on Linux, the FilePath registry value on Windows).
columns.name: install_path

columns.description: Always "-" for ibm_mq: the installer metadata the agent reads carries no edition field.
columns.name: edition

outputs_note: Every row is pipe-delimited. The first row is always `status|<action>|<level>|<reason>` (`level` is `supported`, `constrained` or `unsupported`; `reason` is comma-joined tokens, or `-`). Installation rows follow as `<action>|<title>|<name>|<version>|<install_path>|<edition>`, one per registered installation; the first field is `row_kind` (`status`, or the action name) and is the first column below, and on a status row the next columns carry the action name, the level and the tokens. `supported` with zero rows means none was found at the places read (caveat 1); `constrained` means a read failed or was skipped and the rows may be incomplete, so failure never reads as absent. A field the host did not supply is `-` (the version of an installation whose swidtag directory names no product tag, caveat 4; the edition of every IBM MQ row, which the installer metadata does not carry). Free-text fields go through the shared escaper: a pipe is escaped, a backslash is folded to `/` and a line break to a space, so no value can shift the field count on the server's escape-aware decoder. `middleware` is not in the server's `kKeyValuePlugins` set (`server/core/src/result_parsing.hpp`), so its rows are not decoded as two-cell key and value rows.

privileges.grant: `ibm_mq`: none expected, because the key sits under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE`, which ordinary accounts read
privileges.if_refused: `status|ibm_mq|constrained|windows:middleware:installation_key:permission_denied` (a refused read of the key in either view, the installations the other view listed still being returned, or of an installation's `FilePath` value); `installation_key:unreadable` when the key or an installation's `FilePath` value failed to read in any other way; an unreadable `VRMF` value only blanks that installation's version (`-`), unless no installation that got a row has a `VRMF` value at all (`windows:middleware:vrmf:malformed`, rows kept)
privileges.measured: Measured in an elevated administrator session (account in Administrators, high integrity) on one real IBM MQ 9.4.5.0 install (Windows 10.0.26200, bare metal, 2026-11-24; `docs/samples/windows.txt`); NOT measured as a standard (non-administrator) user, as the service account, on another MQ version, on a 32-bit-only registration or with several installations
privileges.runs_as: agent service account (`NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent` on the packaged service, `docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

privileges.grant: `ibm_mq`: none expected, because `/etc/opt/mqm/mqinst.ini` is world-readable and `/opt/mqm/swidtag` is world-listable and readable
privileges.if_refused: `status|ibm_mq|constrained|linux:middleware:mqinst_ini:permission_denied`; an unreadable `swidtag` directory only blanks that installation's version (`-`). Either way a `constrained` answer reaches the installed-software sync as a status-only section: the stored IBM MQ rows are kept and shown as unconfirmed
privileges.measured: MEASURED on a registered IBM MQ Advanced for Developers 9.4.5.0 install (Ubuntu debs, `ubuntu:24.04` container): `/etc/opt/mqm` is 755 root:root, `mqinst.ini` is 644 root:root, `/opt/mqm/swidtag` is 555 mqm:mqm holding 444 files, and an unprivileged account with no extra groups read the file and listed the directory; the four IBM MQ developer images hold only 444 files in `/opt/mqm/swidtag` (`tests/unit/fixtures/middleware/linux/provenance.txt` and `swidtag.listing`); not measured as `yuzu-agent`, nor on another MQ version or distribution
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account (`yuzu-agent` on the packaged unit), never root by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: Linux and Windows: the read finished with no failure, populated, or none found at the places read (`status|<action>|supported|-` with zero rows)

Linux and Windows: one or more enumeration reads failed, were refused or hit a cap, and the rows returned may be incomplete; the tokens are accumulated and comma-joined in the status row. `<source>` is the table's probe id of the failing read (`mqinst_ini` on Linux, `installation_key` or `vrmf` on Windows) or `walk` (the row, row-text or directory-entry budget) or `mountinfo` (the mount table could not be read in full); `<cause>` is one of the closed set `permission_denied`, `unreadable`, `oversized`, `symlink_refused`, `malformed`, `network_fs_skipped`, `row_cap` or `internal_error`. A failure confined to one item is logged and does not constrain the answer: an unreadable or absent swidtag directory, a refused path or no product tag leaves that row's version as `-`, and a stanza lacking `Name` or `FilePath` beside a usable one is skipped (the table after caveat 5 sets out the full mapping). A file with content but no `Installation:` line, or in which no stanza is usable, is `malformed` and constrains. The bare `internal_error` is a caught exception on any leg: it never crosses the plugin boundary and the command returns 1 (a failed command)

macOS: the leg is not shipped; the action answers `status|<action>|unsupported|macos:planned` and nothing else. `windows:planned` is the same answer for a product whose Windows leg the table declares planned; no product is today

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Every row is server instruction-result data, with the standard retention policy, served over REST `/api/responses`.

**Installed software.** The action feeds the agent's daily installed-software sync (`middleware.ibm_mq`) as ecosystem `ibm_mq`, kind `app`, carrying name, version and publisher only; the install path and edition are not carried. A `constrained` answer is a status-only section that leaves the stored rows in place (caveat 5).
**Not consumed by** TAR, DEX, or metrics.

**Sensitivity.** Rows name installed IBM MQ installations with their version and install path, which is a software inventory for the device. On Windows the name, path and version are registry text: the version is the VRMF string as written and is not shape-checked. On Linux the version is VRM (version.release.modification) read from a file name; the fix-pack level is not carried (a fix pack 9.3.5.1 reports 9.3.5). `name` and `install_path` echo `mqinst.ini` text as found, so a value planted in that file reaches a row after the UTF-8 and pipe scrub (a NUL or an invalid byte reads `?`, which keeps the field's length and boundaries). `mqinst.ini` is trusted as written by root or the MQ installer: its owner and mode are not checked (measured 644 root:root in a 755 root:root directory), so someone who can already write `/etc/opt/mqm` can plant a name, path or version. That gains no authority: the version is digits and dots taken from a file name, and the name and path are inventory text.
**Siblings:** none yet; each further product adds a table row, an action and a `crossplatform.middleware.<id>` definition.
